The operational process at Fashion Forward relies on a first-in-first-out (FIFO) storage system, which creates a significant bottleneck when accessing newer inventory. Because newer items are placed behind older stock, retrieving the latest inventory requires time-consuming reorganization efforts. This inefficiency slows down the shipment process and increases labor costs associated with moving items to access the desired stock. To improve efficiency, the warehouse should consider implementing a system that allows for direct access to newer items, such as a dynamic slotting system or a different storage layout that does not require moving older stock to reach newer arrivals.
